title: Canonical definitions for semilinear exchange reindexing
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], the chosen Cartesian squares of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the pro-etale ordinary and derived operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], compactifications and refinements of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and the specified exchange domains of [def-exchange-projection]. This definition records the following canonical constructions, together with the explicit predicates naming their normalization equations; it asserts none of those equations.

(1) A chosen Cartesian square determines its projection-preserving IsPullback square (finiteMateCartesian). For a Cartesian square h:U'->U, j':U'->V', j:U->V, b:V'->V with j,j' open immersions and finite commutative coefficients A, finiteMateOpenReindexing is j_! b^* ~= h^* j'_!, the uniqueness-of-left-adjoints comparison whose right-adjoint comparison is the canonical section map on the two fibre products. finiteMateDerivedOpenReindexing applies that isomorphism degreewise and localizes, with the canonical derived composition comparisons. The scheme and coefficient universes are retained, including the standard site-size lift; no base-linearity of h,b is imposed.

(2) For constant commutative coefficients B, constantSystem consists of the existing constant ring sheaves and their constant-section pullback isomorphisms. For a ring homomorphism B->C, constantChange is the existing constant-sheaf coefficient map and its canonical square. pullId is the identity pullback comparison, descended from the unit-normalized module map. pushComp is the conjugate of the canonical pullback compositor under the specified pullback/direct-image adjunctions. openComp is degreewise open-extension composition followed by its canonical localization compositor. For a compatible compactification triangle [def-cbc-strict-tower-composition-maps], composition is the proper/open composition arrow: apply the proper mate of its open-square comparison, then the canonical open and proper compositors. For P in the fixed setting and 1<=m<=P.level, lower changes only the coefficient level to m; quotient is the canonical map A_level -> A_m induced by the identity on the valuation ring, with the prescribed site lift; tensorQuotient is the actual derived extension along that quotient.

(3) For an adic coefficient datum d [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and an underlying scheme isomorphism u, PurCompletedReindexingAt(d,u) is the explicit conjunction identifying the ordinary, tower and derived inverse images with exact sectionwise reindexing, the projection-normalized derived-limit comparison, the quotient completion unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and the actual strict reduction tensor comparison and all its transitions. For a chosen Cartesian square whose horizontal maps are isomorphisms, PurCompletedReindexingSquare(d,sq) is the ordinary sectionwise and localized K-injective normalization of its actual ordinary and strict-diagram direct-image mates. These are predicates on the fixed maps, not additional structures choosing maps.

(4) For a compactification and its isomorphism base change, purIntegralReindexingExchange is the ordinary direct-image reindexing mate followed by direct image of the canonical open comparison. With the actual strict reduction and reconstruction maps of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], PurIntegralStrictMapNormalization is the predicate identifying the chosen strict lift with that sectionwise mate before Rlim; PurIntegralStrictHorizontal and PurIntegralStrictVertical are its strict identity/successive-base-change and compatible-tower composition equations; PurIntegralStrictReduction is its square with the actual strict tensor/projection comparisons at every quotient, retaining their fixed corners; PurIntegralCompletedCoherence is the reconstructed identity and both pasting equations. PurStrictIntegralGeometricNormalization(P) is the predicate on separated finite-type k-schemes and their isomorphism base changes saying that the actual strict proper factor, the ordinary open-unit transpose and its completed open factor have these specified normalizations, and that the ordered completed support exchange equals the ordinary proper/open reindexing composite after the specified completion units. The tower composition maps are those of [def-cbc-strict-tower-composition-maps]; origin or completeness restrictions are exactly the domains already specified by those operations. All of these names are transparent exports of the existing constructions and predicates, with every original argument and universe. They add no theorem, arbitrary comparison or choice from existence. The finite normalization, identity, horizontal-pasting, vertical-pasting, composition-invertibility and quotient-coefficient clauses are also named by proposition definitions PurSemilinearFiniteNormalization, PurSemilinearFiniteIdentity, PurSemilinearFiniteHorizontal, PurSemilinearFiniteVertical, PurSemilinearFiniteCompositionIsIso and PurSemilinearFiniteCoefficient: they spell out respectively the specified proper mate/counit and open-unit transpose and ordered composite, the canonical unitor equation, the pullback-compositor pasting equation, the compatible-triangle interchange equation, invertibility of the triangle composition map on a fixed etale-origin input [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and the square with derived A_level -> A_m extension on finite constructible finite-Tor inputs [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. These are predicates, not proofs of the clauses.
